messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: alert=generation-runtime-exceptions count=38 window=5m severity=P1 paging: @ben (on-call)
ben: taking this. seeing a spike in 500s from the model runtime in us-west-2. routing errors and OOMs in the logs. adding context to incident ticket: https://infra.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2026-421
carla: on-call handover note: ben is primary, i'm standby. ping me if we need region failover.
ben: quick snapshot: errors concentrated on pool-gpu-3 nodes, approx 14 hosts reporting similar stack traces. customer impact: some hosted API calls getting 500s -> affecting realtime chat flows for a handful of high-frequency tenants.
alice: thanks — any immediate mitigation we can do? throttling, route to cold pool, or fallback model?
ben: starting temporary reroute to cpu-fallback for low-priority routes, and enabling rate-limit at edge for noisy tenants. will also disable batch-aggregation for the pool to reduce memory pressure.
dave: adding a short-term filter on the log alert to reduce noise while we stabilize. current rule is matching any "RuntimeException" in logs which is too broad.
emma: can we craft a signature for the specific stack trace? the one with `KVCache::alloc` OOM looks distinct.
ben: copying observed stack snippet here for patterning:
```
RuntimeException: failed to allocate KVCache::alloc size=34000000 at model_infer.cpp:422
  at Redwood::KVCache::alloc(Redwood::KVCache*, size_t)
  at Redwood::Serving::Kernel::forward(Serving.cpp:711)
  at ff_backend::infer(request.cpp:89)
```
carla: propose update to the log rule: require both "KVCache::alloc" and "failed to allocate" in the same event, and exclude benign "RuntimeException: tokenizer" entries. also add a 30s suppression window per host.
dave: suggested query (Stackdriver/LogQL style):
```
resource.type="k8s_container" AND
log =~ "KVCache::alloc" AND
log =~ "failed to allocate" AND
NOT log =~ "tokenizer|decode_warning"
| dedup_by(host)
| window(30s)
| count() > 3
```
emma: that looks good. for ES we can use a regex: `/KVCache::alloc.*failed to allocate/` combined with `NOT /tokenizer|decode_warning/`.
ben: applying a temporary stricter rule in the alerting engine (threshold bumped to >5 over 5m but with the KVCache fingerprint). will monitor for the next 10m and then either revert or make permanent.
alice: can we add a quick dashboard panel for this signature? want per-host error counts + memory free metric side-by-side.
carla: creating dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.com/d/err-kvcache. panel: time series count by host, and a heatmap for free_gpu_mem_mb. sharing to #product later.
dave: follow-up action items (post-incident):
- add fingerprinted alert rule (KVCache signature) and reduce sensitivity of generic RuntimeException rule
- implement a host-level suppression of noisy tenants (rate-limit keys)
- add unit tests to log parser to avoid tokenizer false-positives
- run a one-week alert-noise review and adjust thresholds
ben: confirmed customer impact: ~7 tenants saw increased error rates, one (tenant: hyperchat) had degraded sessions for ~12 minutes. support case #CS-876 opened.
emma: scheduling a postmortem sync tomorrow 09:30 PT. invite: @carla @ben @alice @dave + infra-eng.
ben: mitigation status: CPU-fallback routing active, edge rate-limit in place, alert filter deployed. errors dropping.
incident-bot: incident INC-2026-421 transitioned to MONITORING state by ben. SLA impact recorded: partial degradation 00:12:00.
carla: will follow up with a RFC for formalizing log signatures for known failure modes. putting draft in repo: https://git.redwood.com/eng/alerting/rfcs/kvcache-signature.md
alice: nice work team. after the postmortem let's finalize the permanent rule, and consider an automated remediation (drain + rotate) if KVCache OOM pattern recurs.
ben: ack. logging this thread to the incident ticket. closing slack thread once postmortem scheduled.
